facts.subject: 10% of the brain myth. SciAm (Gordon): 'we use virtually every part of the brain… active almost all the time'; brain ~3% of body weight, 20% of energy. MIT McGovern (2024): 'two percent of our body weight… 20 percent of our calories'; 'we use our entire brain every day'; 'Even while we sleep, our entire brain remains intensely active'; William James 1907 'The Energies of Men': 'we are making use of only a small part of our possible mental and physical resources' (no 10% figure); Einstein quote undocumented. -> 2–3% weight, 20% energy.

facts.subject: Azerbaijan National Carpet Museum, Baku seaside park. Founded 1967 (Wikipedia, gpsmycity, Atlas Obscura) on the initiative of carpet artist Latif Karimov (gpsmycity; president.az 'late 1960s'). First exhibition in the Juma Mosque in Icherisheher (Wikipedia, Atlas Obscura; permanent exhibition 1972 per president.az/gpsmycity). Then moved to the former Lenin Museum building (Wikipedia/gpsmycity 1992, Atlas Obscura 1991 -> no year in the reel). New building designed by Austrian architect Franz Janz to look like a rolled carpet (all 4 sources); foundation stone 15 May 2008 (president.az), opened 26 Aug 2014 (Wikipedia, president.az); 'took over six years' (Wikipedia). Collection: more than 10 000 exhibits (Wikipedia; president.az 13 300 / ~15 000 -> say '10 mindən çox'). Largest collection of Azerbaijani carpets in the world (gpsmycity, Atlas Obscura, Wikipedia). 2010: Azerbaijani carpet weaving on UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list (president.az, gpsmycity). NOT used: 'first carpet museum in the world' (only Wikipedia), exact item count, move year.

facts.subject: Baku–Batumi kerosene pipeline. Built 1897–1907 (Georgian Encyclopedia, azerbaijans.com; Wikipedia: State Council decision 23 May 1896, first stage 1906, official opening 24 July 1907 in Tiflis, same date SOCAR Midstream). Length 885 km (Wikipedia) / 829 versts ≈ 885 km (SOCAR, azerbaijans.com) / 863 km (Georgian Encyclopedia) -> say '860 km-dən çox'. Carried kerosene (all; Georgian Encyclopedia 'only refined oil products'). Capacity ~980 000 t/yr (Wikipedia) / 960 000 t (Georgian Enc.) / 800 000 t (SOCAR) -> 'ildə 1 milyon tona yaxın'. 'The world's longest kerosene pipeline' when built (Wikipedia, azerbaijans.com). Mainly 8-inch (200 mm) pipe, 16 pumping stations (Wikipedia only -> not in the voice). Crude oil line Baku–Batumi opened 1930 (Wikipedia 30 Apr 1930; Georgian Enc. Feb 1930). NOT used: designer (Shukhov per Wikipedia vs Taghiyev/Naghiyev per SOCAR — disputed), cost, Mendeleev.
